readMe.title: China Defense-Industrial Atlas — Supplier Scorecards v1.2
readMe.blurb: Additive, source-gated supplier × capability assessments through 2026-08-31. This workbook preserves the legacy Atlas as context and does not replace its broader research-priority ranking.

notes.note: The workbook and extracted import are immutable. Reviewed overlays retain imported score values.
The claimed 1,841 sources and 19 new exact-name entities cannot be reproduced from this workbook and are excluded from current metrics.
Signals are counted from actual signal records; the original 11 included headings or tasks and is replaced by the derived count.
The identity queue is a suggested review set, not a reconstruction of the workbook's unsupported 19-entity flag.

scoringMethod.title: Scoring method and audit gates
scoringMethod.blurb: Inputs are transparent. The v1.2 initial rankings use the displayed weights; scenario columns in Scorecard Ranking allow sensitivity checks but do not silently re-sort the frozen research triage order.

weights.interpretation: Mission/design bottleneck evidence; C4 requires explicit sole/limited-source or requalification support.
U0–U5 lifecycle label; U5 requires fielding/sustainment, not merely award or batch production.
Same capability across documented scope clusters; broad parent/module affiliation is insufficient.
Demonstrated technical differentiation, validation, or observable performance evidence.
Avoids turning technical importance into a monopoly claim.

weights.weight: U3+ has qualification, batch, delivery, production, or fielding language
weights.interpretation: Award / R&D / demonstration are not delivery.

weights.weight: Pre-award and product-marketing entries cannot rank
weights.interpretation: Prevents candidate suppliers from appearing as completed suppliers.

weights.weight: Credit comes from source text, not just Atlas tags
weights.interpretation: Prevents parent or shared module labels from inflating leverage.

weights.weight: Blank unless direct source supports a barrier or dependency

evidenceFactors.hardBoundary: Lead or weak context cannot rank.
Single source or attributed capability; no verified rank.
Repeated direct evidence / corroboration, with entity resolution.
Lifecycle evidence or independently corroborated direct source chain.

chart.plain: A working chart of the capability nodes a robotic or unmanned military system depends on, from sensors to production tooling. Each node lists the firms the scorecard package evidences against it. A node with no evidence is shown as empty, not filled by inference.

cases.summary: Separate the robot manufacturer, integration partner and end user. Customer reporting corroborates the application, while OEM identification remains supplier-attributed.
cases.whatMatters: Civilian operating experience and follow-on deliveries are useful evidence of adoption. A pilot does not establish network-wide rollout.
cases.unknown: Exact units, contracting entity, acceptance dates, utilization and military connections are not established by these sources.
cases.nextEvidence: SP Group acceptance or asset records naming X30, the contracting integrator and phase-two quantities.
cases.decision: Would independently verify the OEM/customer chain and distinguish experimentation from sustained deployment.
cases.counterEvidence: A customer record naming another platform or a discontinued pilot would change the integration assessment.

cases.title: Unitree: commercial platform and separate military observation
cases.summary: Go2 availability and SDK access are documented. CCTV's military quadrupeds remain unidentified equipment in this collection.
cases.whatMatters: Commercial adaptability, model identification, third-party integration and direct military contracting are four different claims.
cases.unknown: The military robots' OEM, model, seller, integrator, contract and fielding scale are unknown.
cases.nextEvidence: A dated procurement or acceptance record naming manufacturer, model, seller and buyer; assess imagery attribution separately.
cases.decision: Would support a specific supply relationship rather than inferring one from appearance or product availability.
cases.counterEvidence: A different manufacturer or an intermediary purchase would change OEM attribution or direct-contract claims.

cases.title: Jingpin: complete robots, new modules and civilian transfer
cases.summary: Split established business activity from component development and management's military-to-civilian account. The evidence describes FY2024.
cases.whatMatters: Product families at different stages need separate assessments. Reported equivalent output cannot measure robot deliveries.
cases.unknown: Model-level unit counts, external module sales and independently confirmed civilian transfer remain unestablished.
cases.nextEvidence: Later annual filings and customer-side acceptance, separated into complete robots, external components and civilian manufacturing.
cases.decision: Would show whether module development became external supply and whether civilian transfer generated accepted products.
cases.counterEvidence: Discontinued development or customer rejection would weaken the transfer and component-commercialization assessments.

cases.title: Xirui: awarded shipyard automation
cases.summary: Two separate final workstation awards name a supplier and purchaser. Delivery, productive use and naval end use remain unknown.
cases.whatMatters: RMB10.37m is the sum of two award values. It is not installed capacity, supplier revenue or evidence of naval production.
cases.unknown: Installation, acceptance, utilization, component manufacturers and vessel/program allocation are not disclosed.
cases.nextEvidence: Purchaser commissioning or acceptance notices for tender numbers CSSC-03-251066-031 and CSSC-03-251066-030.
cases.decision: Would move the relationship beyond award and permit a bounded claim about productive use.
cases.counterEvidence: Cancellation, delayed acceptance or a different delivered scope would change the capacity assessment.

cases.title: Estun: ownership enters, control ends, holding exits
cases.summary: The ownership route is historical. Control ended in June 2025; the remaining stake was sold in November.
cases.whatMatters: Ownership is dated separately from supply. A former defense affiliate must not be presented as a current controlled subsidiary.
cases.unknown: Current product customers and any continuing Estun–Shuguang technical or supply ties require separate verification.
cases.nextEvidence: Buyer-side subsequent filings, current corporate registration and dated post-disposal supply contracts.
cases.decision: Would establish the post-sale ownership and distinguish historical affiliation from continuing commercial ties.
cases.counterEvidence: A later acquisition could change ownership again; the 2025 exit alone cannot settle later relationships.

cases.title: Siasun: civil work inside an aerospace group
cases.summary: The 2015 source identifies a civil-aircraft counterparty and planned metal-printing research involving C919.
cases.whatMatters: A defense-group name does not determine project end use. Existing cooperation and proposed equipment use have different states.
cases.unknown: Equipment delivery, acceptance, completed research and later production use are not established.
cases.nextEvidence: Customer-side agreement or completion/acceptance record identifying the equipment and civil-aircraft project.
cases.decision: Would establish whether the proposed work occurred and its achieved result.
cases.counterEvidence: A separate military contract would be a new relationship, not a reason to relabel this civil-aircraft case.

bibliography.what_it_is_good_for: Named product categories, batch production, customer class, qualifications, capacity, and sometimes limited-source language.

bibliography.what_it_is_good_for: Named winner, buyer, project scope, result state, date, and disclosed price for specific production or equipment procurements.
bibliography.what_it_cannot_prove_alone: A shipyard production-equipment award does not establish a weapon component relationship or enterprise-wide revenue.

bibliography.what_it_is_good_for: Demand shape, technical requirements, bid/pre-award/final-state distinctions, and named component stacks.
bibliography.what_it_cannot_prove_alone: Intent, candidates, or first-ranked notices cannot be treated as award, delivery, fielding, or repeat supply without final proof.

bibliography.what_it_is_good_for: Attributed capability, provenance, local incubation, test participation, and sometimes installed-base claims.
bibliography.what_it_cannot_prove_alone: They are not independent evidence of contract completion, program integration, or production volumes when claims are company-attributed.

bibliography.what_it_is_good_for: Named historical exports/reexports, tools, direct counterparties, values, and known time windows.
